requirements.requirement: Run a nightly backup of node2:/srv/inventory/data to node1 as a dated archive under /var/backups/inventory.
requirements.summary: Node1 has an active, enabled cron daemon and a 02:15 daily entry invoking the backup script. The script pulls from node2, writes inventory-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz under the required destination, and successful runs produced a valid archive before and after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last seven days of dated inventory archives.
requirements.summary: The installed cleanup rule deletes matching archives at age seven days or greater using -mtime +6. A bounded eight-day-old test archive was created, then directly shown to be removed by a backup run.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 before and after execution. The implementation used already installed EL9 utilities, and final package-health observations were clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The restart protocol is also strong for both managed nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart scheduling, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered services and persisted configuration, and successful post-restart end-to-end backup behavior.
limitations: No naturally timed 02:15 cron invocation was observed; automation is supported by the installed cron entry, active/enabled crond, and successful manual execution of the identical script.

The source path was absent initially and was created empty. Captured archives therefore contain only data/ and do not demonstrate preservation of representative inventory file contents, although the end-to-end archive stream and integrity checks succeeded.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Persistent changes—backup directories, restricted SSH credentials and helper, host resolution, backup script, and cron entry—have clear task roles. The synthetic old archive was bounded verification data and was removed during the same test. The transient reboot units and restarts were required by the provider-wide restart protocol. Failed crond/grep probes and interrupted commands do not show harmful mutations. Lifecycle snapshots show no failed services, new listening sockets, package damage, or unexplained temporary residue after execution.
